title: Clean Substrings
solution: An operation is only useful when it inverts a whole maximal run, which merges it with its neighbours and removes up to 2 runs (1 at an end), so a string with k runs has beauty floor(k/2) = ceil(b/2), where b = k-1 is the number of adjacent unequal positions. Summing over substrings, ceil(b/2) = (b + [b odd])/2. The sum of b over all substrings is the contribution of each boundary j (s_j != s_{j+1}): j*(n-j). The parity of b equals [s_l != s_r], so the number of substrings with odd b is cnt0*cnt1. Hence power = (sum_j [s_j!=s_{j+1}]*j*(n-j) + cnt0*cnt1)/2. Flipping s_i only toggles boundaries i-1 and i and shifts cnt0/cnt1, so each update is O(1); total O(n+q).
solution_check: Python implementation of the closed formula reproduced all four sample outputs exactly (2 2 / 7 5 5 / 36 23 22 25 26 / 61 66 41 35 59 60).

rejected_patterns.reason: The beauty = floor(runs/2) fact is a structural observation (each op removes at most 2 run boundaries, and whole-run inversion achieves it), not a greedy algorithm; the solution is pure contribution counting with O(1) updates. Searching 'greedy' should not surface this.

notes.solver: Key insight: beauty = floor(runs/2) (greedy/exchange reasoning on runs), then per-boundary contribution j*(n-j) plus an odd-parity correction cnt0*cnt1 via s_l xor s_r. No segment tree needed since each flip changes O(1) terms; segment-tree/fenwick rejected as labels. 'greedy' is low-confidence: it only justifies the beauty formula, not the counting.
notes.skeptic: Brute-force BFS confirmed beauty = floor(runs/2) for all binary strings up to length 10; closed formula power = (sum over boundaries j of j*(n-j) + cnt0*cnt1)/2 matched O(n^2) brute force on 500 random strings and reproduced all four sample outputs. Each flip changes only boundaries i-1, i and cnt0/cnt1, so O(1) per query; no segment tree/fenwick needed. 'counting' kept as secondary (pairs with s_l != s_r = cnt0*cnt1); summary is accurate, ~60 words, includes n,q constraints.
